overview: Intellia Therapeutics (NTLA) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts-based genome editing company co-founded in 2014 by Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna. It develops in vivo CRISPR/Cas9 therapies delivered by lipid nanoparticles to the liver, aiming for one-time, potentially curative treatments.

The nearest-term asset is lonvo-z (NTLA-2002) for hereditary angioedema (HAE). In the Phase 3 HAELO trial, a single infusion reduced attacks by 87% versus placebo, met all key secondary endpoints and was published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Intellia expects FDA acceptance of the BLA in 2H 2026 and a U.S. launch in 1H 2027 — which would make it the first in vivo CRISPR therapy on the market.

The larger opportunity is nex-z (NTLA-2001) for transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis, partnered with Regeneron. Phase 3 MAGNITUDE (cardiomyopathy) and MAGNITUDE-2 (polyneuropathy) enrollment was paused over liver safety and has since resumed; new genomic analysis links a specific HLA allele to elevated liver enzymes, which could help manage the risk.

Investor thesis: NTLA is a bet that one-time gene editing can displace chronic therapies. A clean lonvo-z launch would validate the platform commercially, while nex-z offers much larger upside in ATTR if the safety question is resolved. The stock has fallen sharply from its highs as investors weigh the nex-z safety overhang and competition from established ATTR drugs.

advantage: One-time treatment versus lifelong dosing. Lonvo-z's 87% attack reduction from a single infusion is a compelling pitch to HAE patients tired of chronic injections or daily pills.

catalysts.title: Lonvo-z BLA Acceptance
catalysts.description: FDA acceptance of the HAE filing and assignment of a PDUFA date.

catalysts.title: MAGNITUDE-2 Enrollment Complete
catalysts.description: Completion of the nex-z Phase 3 polyneuropathy trial enrollment.

catalysts.title: Lonvo-z U.S. Launch
catalysts.description: First commercial in vivo CRISPR therapy; early uptake will set the tone for the platform.

catalysts.title: Nex-z Safety Updates
catalysts.description: Any new liver safety signals in MAGNITUDE trials would weigh heavily on the stock.

risks.title: Nex-z Liver Safety
risks.description: Phase 3 enrollment was previously paused over liver safety; any recurrence could threaten the ATTR program.

risks.title: Commercial Execution
risks.description: Intellia has never launched a product; pricing and reimbursement for a one-time gene therapy are untested in HAE.

risks.title: Competition
risks.description: Established ATTR drugs (Amvuttra, Attruby, tafamidis) and multiple HAE options set a high bar.

risks.title: Cash Burn
risks.description: Q2 2026 net loss of $106.6M; guidance funds operations into 2028, but a launch plus Phase 3 trials are expensive.

risks.title: Regulatory
risks.description: First-of-kind in vivo editing filing may draw extra FDA scrutiny on long-term safety follow-up.

partners.name: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals
partners.description: Shares development costs and economics for nex-z in ATTR amyloidosis.

partners.name: Kyverna Therapeutics
partners.description: Allogeneic CD19 CAR-T for B cell-mediated autoimmune diseases.

interpretation: $628M in cash (bolstered by a $195M April 2026 offering) is guided to last at least into 2028, past the expected lonvo-z launch. The runway shown here assumes the latest quarter's cash burn continues unchanged; management's guidance also factors in expected revenue and cost savings.
